finding.claim: Unauthenticated blind SSRF via avatarUrl; the only check is an https:// prefix, and axios follows redirects to arbitrary hosts, including internal and http:// targets.

trace.note: unauthenticated POST /profile/avatar route; no auth middleware in this file
only check: typeof string and startsWith('https://')
axios.get follows redirects by default, no host/IP filter, no DNS pinning
only byte length returned, so attacker gets a status/length oracle

finding.guards_checked: https:// prefix only; no host or IP blocklist; no maxRedirects:0; no post-redirect scheme or host check; no DNS pinning; no auth middleware. /users/:id (server.js:20) checked and not reported: fixed host USER_SVC, id is encodeURIComponent'd.

verdict.guard_found: none. server.js:11 checks only typeof string and startsWith("https://"), which is a prefix check and does not close the finding. No host or IP allowlist, no maxRedirects:0, and no post-redirect check appear at server.js:14. server.js:5 is only express.json(), and no auth middleware is applied to the route at server.js:9. The directory contains only server.js.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: req.body.avatarUrl at server.js:10 is attacker-controlled on an unauthenticated POST route (server.js:9), the only check at server.js:11 is an https:// prefix, and axios.get at server.js:14 follows redirects to arbitrary hosts with no host filter.
